title: Two Records, One Wobble, and the 14th Hole for Everybody Else
title_candidates: Two Records, One Wobble, and the 14th Hole for Everybody Else
The Boavista Standard: Mullin Sets the Bar, Then Clears It Again
Baker Led for Twenty-One Holes. Mullin Needed Three.
The Fourteenth Will See You Now
theme: On a course none of them had ever seen, David Mullin twice posted the best round TEG had yet recorded — and the only man who got close, Jon Baker, held the Trophy lead for barely a round before losing it in the first three holes of R3. Around them, Boavista's par-3 14th quietly collected 8s and 9s from everyone else.
tone: house — faithful, tongue-in-cheek, insider-facing; ribbing earned by the scorecards, never invented
opening_hook: Open on R3, hole 3: Baker three clear overnight and already 12 shots to par through five; Mullin bogeys the par-5 3rd for a net par (b07) and takes an outright lead he never gives back — then loop back to R1 to explain how a three-shot deficit came to be so easily reversed.
foreshadow: Mullin's R1 net +0 (b02) and +20 gross (b03) were the best rounds TEG had ever seen — a bar he would end up having to clear a second time
The par-3 14th at Boavista collected an 8 from Neumann, an 8 from Meller and a 9 from Williams on day one alone
Baker's near-record rounds (+4, then +1) came with a habit hidden in the margins: quadruple bogeys, at the 17th, the 12th, the 18th
Meller was outright last by the 3rd hole of the tournament and never moved from bottom of any round

competitions.name: Trophy (Net VP)
competitions.winner_or_loser: David Mullin (winner, +6, by 7 from Jon Baker)
competitions.how: Mullin opened with net +0 (b02), the best round in TEG history to date, for a four-shot lead. He then coughed it up in R2 — ten shots to par across 16-17-18 (b43) turned a +8 round into a handover, and Baker, with a +1 (b10) built on a three-hole burst at 6-7-8 (b41), went three clear. The reign lasted 18 holes: Baker bled 12 shots over the first five holes of R3 (b24) while Mullin bogeyed the par-5 3rd for a net par and the outright lead (b07). Mullin's closing -2 (b04) — again the best round TEG had recorded — turned a three-shot deficit into a seven-shot win (b01).

competitions.name: Green Jacket (Gross)
competitions.winner_or_loser: David Mullin (winner, +66, by 11 from Stuart Neumann)
competitions.how: Effectively over by tea on day one: Mullin's +20 (b03) was the best gross round in TEG history to date and opened a nine-shot cushion. His R2 +28 (b12) was still third-best all-time and kept him eight clear despite the closing collapse; his R3 +18 (b05) reset the record again and stretched the margin to eleven (b06). Neumann's two second-best-ever gross rounds (b09, b11) were plenty good enough for the runner-up spot and nowhere near enough for the Jacket — the last Jacket lead change came on hole 5 of R1.

competitions.name: Wooden Spoon
competitions.how: Decided almost immediately: Meller was outright bottom by the 3rd hole of R1 and stayed there after all three rounds. The damage was the 11th-to-15th stretch on day one — 20 shots gone in five holes (b16), including a quintuple at the 14th — for a +24 round. He improved every day (+24, +13, +2) and signed off with a +20 gross (b13), then the second-best gross round in TEG history, but the Spoon had been settled 54 holes earlier.

rounds.chosen_headline: Ten Shots in Three Holes — Mullin Gift-Wraps the Lead
rounds.angle: Mullin's third-best-ever gross round (b12) is undone by 16, 17 and 18 (b43); Baker's +1 (b10) puts him three clear, while Neumann posts another near-record gross and Boavista's 14th takes a second 8 off him.

headline_candidates: Baker Leads by Three, Trails by the Third
Mullin's -2 and the Shortest Reign in TEG History
Meller's Consolation Prize: A Record-Book Round and a Wooden Spoon
rounds.chosen_headline: Baker Leads by Three, Trails by the Third
rounds.angle: Baker gives away 12 shots in five holes (b24) before he is properly awake; Mullin's -2 (b04) and +18 gross (b05) rewrite both record lines again, and behind them Meller finally plays the golf he came for (b13) with nothing left to save.

players.arc: Sets the TEG standard on day one, hands it back over the last three holes of R2, then reclaims it inside three holes of R3 and wins both the Trophy by 7 and the Jacket by 11 — four separate TEG-best round marks in three days on a course he had never seen.

Two of the best net rounds TEG had recorded (+4, +1), a lead of three going into the last day, and then 12 shots to par in the first five holes of R3 — a tragic arc compressed into an hour, finishing runner-up by seven.

The most consistent striker of the ball after Mullin — second-best-ever gross rounds in both R1 and R2 — and Jacket runner-up by 11, with two quintuple bogeys at the same par-3 14th to show for his trouble.

Last after every round and Spoon-bound by the 3rd hole of the tournament, yet the only man in the field to improve in every round (+24, +13, +2), signing off with what was then the second-best gross round in TEG history.
Briefly leading on hole 2 of the entire TEG, then the back nine of R1 relieved him of 22 shots in seven holes, including a 9 at the 14th — his 105 in R3 was his best of the three.

venue_notes: TEG's first trip to the Algarve, and Boavista (Lagos) staged all three rounds — Howard Swan parkland, Atlantic views, and a layout that splits into two distinct halves, which is a polite way of saying the back nine did most of the eating (Meller 11-15, Williams 12-18, Neumann 13-17, all in R1). A new course for TEG, so no prior form for anyone and every mark set here becomes the Boavista benchmark. Thread the par-3 14th as the running character: three 8s and a 9 across the week, and both of Neumann's worst holes of the tournament. Use the same-course-three-days angle to explain why the field improved and the scores tightened while Mullin simply got better.
course_history_notes: First visit to Boavista for all five players — no prior form to lean on, which makes Mullin's back-to-back record rounds on unfamiliar ground the more notable.
Mullin's best Boavista gross was his 89 in R3; Neumann's 92 (R3), Meller's 91 (R3), Baker's 100 (R2) and Williams's 105 (R3) set the rest of the founding benchmarks at the course.
Meller's best Boavista round (91 gross, R3) arrived two days after the Spoon had effectively been settled.
decisive_moments: Trophy: R3 H3 — Mullin bogeys the par-5 3rd for a net par (b07) while Baker plays the opening five in 12 over (b24); a three-shot overnight deficit becomes an outright lead never surrendered.
Green Jacket: R1 — Mullin's +20 gross (b03), then the best gross round in TEG history, opens a nine-shot cushion after 18 holes; the Jacket lead never changes hands again (b06).
Wooden Spoon: R1 holes 11-15 — Meller bleeds 20 shots in five holes (b16) for a +24 round, sitting bottom by the 3rd hole of the tournament and after every round thereafter (b19).

payoffs.seed: Mullin's R1 +0 / +20 gross set the TEG bar
payoffs.payoff: He has to clear his own bar to win: -2 net (b04) and +18 gross (b05) rewrite both marks again and turn a deficit into a seven-shot victory.

payoffs.seed: The par-3 14th collecting 8s and 9s on day one
payoffs.payoff: Neumann posts a second quintuple bogey there in R2 (b18), sealing the 14th as the week's shared enemy — the hole that took shots off everyone except the winner.

payoffs.seed: Baker's near-record rounds hid recurring quadruple bogeys
payoffs.payoff: The habit metastasises into the opening five holes of R3 — 12 shots to par (b24) — costing him the lead by the 3rd and the Trophy by seven.

payoffs.seed: Meller bottom by the 3rd hole of the tournament
payoffs.resolves_in: How the three were decided / Wooden Spoon
payoffs.payoff: He improves in every round and closes with a then TEG-second-best +20 gross (b13), but the Spoon (b19) was decided 54 holes earlier — the best round of his week counted for nothing.

vehicle_fit_response.note: The Jacket procession is real but it is texture, not the frame: the Trophy changed hands four times outright, including a decisive takeover at R3 H3, so the report is framed on the Mullin/Baker dual narrative with Baker's R3 collapse as the tragic strand.
